claims.statement: The EU Data Act gives connected-product users access to generated data and permits sharing with third parties of their choice in defined circumstances.
Required access can include relevant metadata in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format, while security, personal-data, and trade-secret constraints remain binding.
Demand hypothesis: mixed-fleet industrial users will buy a neutral mandate and connector layer rather than manage each OEM request themselves.

contrary_evidence: The Data Act does not itself create a legal basis for sharing personal data and permits protections for security and trade secrets.
Some connected products may store no remotely accessible useful data, making a mandate commercially empty.

economics.acquisition_route: Demand hypothesis: two industrial energy or maintenance partners can provide the first 10 paid sites
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 250 sites at 2500 PLN monthly yields 7.5m PLN ARR; at 20% EBITDA and a 4x EBITDA value, founder equity could exceed 5m PLN in 4-6 years without counting distributions
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly for a six-month narrow-equipment pilot; implementation support can later be delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 75-85% software gross margin after the main OEM connectors stabilize; early integrations are service-heavy
economics.payback: Economics hypothesis: recover initial capital within 12-18 months at 10 sites averaging 2500 PLN monthly after direct integration costs
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 4000-12000 PLN onboarding per site plus 1500-4000 PLN monthly and usage charges
economics.retention_or_repeat: Continuous data delivery, mandate renewals, audit evidence, and additional approved use cases create recurring use

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable OEM connectors, resolved access playbooks, and a growing graph of verified users, assets, and approved recipients
fingerprint.customer: Polish and EU factories operating mixed fleets of connected production, HVAC, and energy equipment
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Energy auditors, maintenance integrators, industrial insurers, and targeted outreach to plant technical managers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Permission registry, OEM request workflow, connector layer, audit log, and approved-recipient workspace sold as SaaS plus onboarding
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The asset user pays at mandate onboarding and monthly per connected site or asset
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An owner needs data for an aftermarket service but the OEM portal, format, mandate, and trade-secret boundaries differ by asset

founder_fit: Direct use of data engineering and AI automation
Polish industrial entry with EU expansion potential
risks: Unclear user status for leased or jointly operated assets

structure.commercial_archetype: Permissioned data trustee and vertical SaaS
structure.control_point: Verified asset-user mandate plus the normalized connector and audit layer
structure.critical_dependency: The customer must qualify as the connected-product user and useful data must be readily available without prohibited disclosure

thesis: A factory appoints the service as its permissioned Data Act access agent; the service retrieves non-personal machine data, normalizes it, and routes it to approved maintenance, energy, or insurance vendors. Demand hypothesis: multi-brand plants will pay to avoid repeating OEM access negotiations and connector work.
title: Industrial Connected-Asset Data Mandate Hub
uncertainties: Plant willingness to appoint an external agent
